The summation identity yields T_m(u)=-1/4+O(m^(-1/2)) uniformly on the specified u ranges. Stirling and -1/Gamma(-u)=u(1+O(u)) give both constants and profile. The t=1 evaluation implies only a liminf lower bound for the full [-m,m] norm. Independently evaluated exact products/high-precision sums for m=20,50,100,250: at u=0.4 the normalized asymptotic ratios are 1.05662,1.02245,1.01119,1.00447, and T approaches -1/4; log-layer numerical convergence is slower but consistent. Source checker.py was read; its barycentric and nodal product formulas are independently structured. No extrapolation of finite results to infinity was made.

value.rationale: The sign interpolant is a canonical complete Krawtchouk projection. The exact moving-edge asymptotic locates and quantifies exponential instability invisible in the known fixed-origin Gibbs profile, and provides an explicit nontrivial lower bound on a natural expanding-interval norm. It is a motivated spectral/interpolation boundary-layer fact, not an arbitrary numerical slice; lack of a global upper bound is carefully stated.

final_claim: The complete symmetric Krawtchouk sign interpolant F_2m has fixed-distance moving-edge asymptotic (-1)^m F_2m(m-u) ~ 4^m m^(-u-5/2) [-1/(2^(u+1) sqrt(pi) Gamma(-u))] for 0<u<1, and the logarithmic layer u=t/log m converges, after m^(5/2)log(m)/4^m normalization, to t exp(-t)/(2 sqrt(pi)) locally uniformly for t>0. Its profile peak gives a rigorous lower bound for the global interval norm, with no global upper-bound claim.
